key_highlights: ASX sheds $90bn in a week as rate-rise fears and oil price surge pressure miners and banks
Iron ore enters 'bloodletting' phase, hitting BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX materially
AUD smashed on growth scare, compounding pressure on importers and rate-sensitive sectors
Oil explodes as price suppression fails; fuel prices to rise 30c, feeding inflation concerns
RBA flagged rental inflation as key concern, complicating rate path
ANZ.AX axed 3,500 jobs; restructuring plan faces long execution horizon
Housing: high-end prices crash while affordable end resilient; no spring bounce in auctions
Mining cap raises intensify (Canaccord-led), signalling sector stress
Australia softens gas supply rules, easing Asian energy fears; Santos preservation noted
Superannuation reform debate intensifies with One Nation proposals and structural critiques

sectors.trend: Sharp negative. Iron ore bloodletting underway; oil surge benefits energy names but broad mining cap raises signal distress. Gold under pressure ('gold schmould'). Small-caps (PolarX, Sunstone, Manuka, Aruma, Gateway WA) showing relative strength.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face near-term downside on iron ore. Energy (Santos, Woodside) supported by oil surge and softened gas rules. Lithium (Standard Lithium SLI) clearing hurdles offers selective upside. Gold miners (Kuniko, Gateway WA) in early exploration phase.

sectors.trend: Negative. Rising bond yields and rate fears pressure valuations. ANZ.AX restructuring (3,500 job cuts) signals margin pressure. Superannuation reform debate adds policy uncertainty.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX face headwinds from yield curve steepening and credit concerns. Superannuation populism (One Nation) could disrupt fund flows. Defensive positioning warranted.

sectors.trend: Positive. Oil 'explodes' as suppression fails; fuel prices to rise 30c. Shell divesting US gas plant ($715m) signals global portfolio reshuffle. Australia softens gas export rules, supporting Santos and Woodside.
sectors.implications: Santos (STO.AX), Woodside (WDS.AX) benefit from oil surge and policy support. Costamare (CMDB) bulker rebound bet adds shipping exposure. Inflation pass-through risk to consumers.

sectors.trend: Mixed-negative. Woolworths (WES.AX) price-freeze breach undermines consumer confidence. Businesses 'fear for their future'. Housing correction may boost first-home buyers but high-end crash hurts discretionary spend.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, CSL.AX (healthcare defensive) relatively resilient. Consumer discretionary under pressure. Tax burden ('drowning in taxes') weighs on disposable income.

sectors.trend: Mixed. IREN (IREN.AX) falls as investors demand AI proof. HIVE scales AI cloud. OpenAI security breach raises cyber risk. Skyworks/Qorvo merger ($22bn) signals semiconductor consolidation.
sectors.implications: IREN.AX needs execution proof. HIVE (HIVE.AX) early-stage. Cybersecurity spend likely to rise. ASX tech remains small-cap dominated.

sectors.trend: Negative at high end, resilient at affordable end. Housing prices crashing at top; first-home buyers surging. RBA rental inflation concern. NZ correction still running. Migrant-driven demand debate ongoing.
sectors.implications: REITs (GP.AX, SPG.AX) face rental yield pressure. Developer names under stress. Affordable housing policy support possible. Leith Van Onselen warns of further falls.

key_themes: Iron ore price collapse driving ASX 200 sell-off
Oil surge and fuel inflation feeding RBA rate uncertainty
AUD weakness amplifying import costs and equity outflows
Mining sector cap-raise wave signalling capital stress
Housing bifurcation: high-end crash vs affordable resilience
Energy policy shift (gas rules) supporting domestic producers

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; diversify into gold and energy
Favour fixed-income and dividend-paying defensives; avoid rate-sensitive REITs
Hedge AUD exposure; favour export-oriented miners and energy
Monitor CPI pass-through; favour energy producers over transport/consumer
Monitor One Nation proposals; assess impact on fund managers and banks
Avoid small-cap miners in active cap raises; wait for post-dilution clarity

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight energy producers on oil surge and gas policy support
opportunities.rationale: Oil 'explodes', fuel prices rising 30c, Australia softens gas rules; Santos/Woodside benefit structurally

opportunities.recommendation: Selective gold exposure on safe-haven rotation
opportunities.rationale: Growth scare and AUD weakness support gold; Kuniko and Gateway WA in early exploration with upside
Standard Lithium clears key hurdles; Critical Resources battery tech validates; critical resources theme intact

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore / large-cap mining exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore 'bloodletting' underway; $90bn ASX loss driven by miners; cap raises signal distress

defensive_moves.recommendation: Defensive tilt to healthcare and consumer staples
defensive_moves.rationale: CSL.AX, WES.AX offer relative stability amid growth scare and rate uncertainty

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid high-end property and rate-sensitive REITs
defensive_moves.rationale: Steepest price falls at top end; RBA rental inflation concern; further correction likely

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. ASX likely to extend losses on iron ore weakness, AUD pressure, and rate fears. Oil surge provides partial offset via energy. Expect volatility around RBA commentary and CPI data. $90bn weekly loss suggests further downside unless iron ore stabilises.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. Housing correction may stabilise; energy transition and critical resources offer structural themes. Superannuation reform, if constructive, could boost long-term fund flows. Iron ore oversupply risk persists but energy transition supports copper/lithium.
